Everything you see here is Freedoom. Every sprite, every colour, every floor is the Freedoom project's artwork, made over twenty years by volunteers and given away freely. This app draws it and does nothing else with it: without their work there would be nothing to show, because the alternative was shipping game data that is not ours to give. Freedoom is a complete free game in its own right, and it deserves to be played, not only borrowed from.

Free, no adverts, no network access, no data collected, and no permissions requested.

Back in 2011 James Gittins put the fight itself on your home screen, and a lot of us left it running there for years. It stopped installing on modern Android long ago. This is not a port or a revival: no code or asset is shared, everything here was written from nothing, and the artwork is Freedoom's. What carried over is the idea, and it deserved to still work. Thanks, James.

The movement, the timings and the creature values are read from the linuxdoom-1.10 source release, which is why this app is GPL-2.0. Every such value carries a comment naming the file and symbol it came from.

This project is independent. Neither the Freedoom project nor any other rights holder endorses or is involved in it.
